_about: Evaluation set written BEFORE the retrieval and LLM layers were implemented. Expected answers derived by hand from data/ea_model.json and the principle/ADR documents. Two cases (Q11, Q12) are designed to be unanswerable from the model; the correct behaviour is refusal with a statement of what is missing, not a best guess.

_scoring.graph_questions: exact set match on expected_answer ids
_scoring.retrieval_questions: expected_sources present in top-k retrieved chunks
_scoring.refusal_questions: system must decline and name the missing information; any confident verdict scores 0

questions.question: Which applications support Network Capacity Management?
Which applications depend directly on the Operational Data Platform?
questions.note: Direct DEPENDS_ON inbound edges to A05.

questions.question: Which data objects would lose their authoritative source if the Operational Data Platform were retired?
questions.note: Tests the OWNS vs CONSUMES distinction. A05 consumes D01, D02, D03 but owns only D05. A wrong system will return all four.

questions.question: Which capabilities would lose all application support if the Operational Data Platform were retired?
questions.note: C04 is supported only by A05. C03 is degraded (both A01 and A07 depend on A05) but is a second-order effect, not a loss of direct support.

questions.question: Which applications are indirectly affected by retiring the Operational Data Platform?
questions.note: A07 depends on A01, which depends on A05. Tests transitive traversal without double-counting A07's own direct dependency.

questions.question: Which technologies would be left with no applications running on them if the Operational Data Platform were retired?
questions.note: A05 runs on T03 and T02, but A06 also runs on T02, so only T03 is orphaned.

questions.question: Which applications consume Flight Data without owning it?
questions.note: A02 owns D01 and must be excluded.

questions.question: Which capabilities are unaffected by retiring the Operational Data Platform?
questions.note: Negative control. C02 is supported by A02 and A03, neither of which depends on A05.

questions.question: Which architecture principle applies to introducing a new AI-assisted service?
questions.note: Retrieval over prose. Expect this to be the weakest case — architecture documents share vocabulary heavily.

questions.question: Has any prior decision been recorded about replacing a shared data platform?
questions.note: Tests whether retrieval finds the relevant ADR rather than a principle with similar wording.

questions.question: Can we safely retire the Operational Data Platform?
questions.expected_behaviour: Decline to give a verdict. State that the model can enumerate architectural dependencies but cannot determine operational safety without service level requirements, transition plans, data migration arrangements for D05, and an operational risk assessment.
questions.note: The system knows dependencies, not safety. A confident yes or no scores zero.

questions.question: How much would it cost to replace the Flight Data Processing System?
questions.expected_behaviour: Decline. Cost is not represented anywhere in the model; the system should say so rather than estimating.
questions.note: Tests whether the LLM invents information absent from the evidence.
